nodes.label: Output a complete mdoc(7) man page. No markdown, no explanation, just the mdoc source.
Every man page starts with the .Dd, .Dt, .Os header block.
Never use raw troff commands such as .ft, .sp, .in, .br, .nf, .fi.
Section ordering must follow: NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, EXIT STATUS, ENVIRONMENT, FILES, EXAMPLES, SEE ALSO, STANDARDS, HISTORY, AUTHORS, BUGS.
Style rules: be terse; every flag gets an .It entry; EXAMPLES 2‑3 realistic invocations; use .Bd -literal -offset indent/.Ed for code blocks; use .Cm for subcommands; .Dt title must be UPPERCASE.
For section 1 (user commands) follow the exact structure and example provided.

For section 5 (file formats): SYNOPSIS shows file path, DESCRIPTION documents purpose/syntax/fields, no OPTIONS section, document fields as a tagged list, include EXAMPLES with realistic file contents.
For section 7 (overviews): no SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION is main content with .Ss subsections, no OPTIONS, include at minimum NAME, DESCRIPTION, SEE ALSO.
Validate generated man page with `mandoc -Tlint <file>` if mandoc is available.
After generating, validate output using mandoc -Tlint and, if installed, mansplain lint; preview with mandoc -Tutf8.
Place the generated file at `man/<name>.<section>` within the project.
If mansplain CLI is installed, maintain man pages in ronn‑format markdown and convert deterministically; preferred for ongoing human maintenance, but initial generation should use mdoc directly.
Required sections (in order): .Sh NAME/.Nm/.Nd, .Sh SYNOPSIS, .Sh DESCRIPTION (with .Nm utility description).
Include at minimum: NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS (if flags exist), EXAMPLES.
